name: v5-makers
framing: Fill 16:9 with a centered cover crop, no pillarboxing; CSS object-fit cover adapts the film to the viewport. Preserve the existing shot order, durations, monochrome grade, and dissolves.

shots.title: Arts And Crafts, Kyoto — brush painting on silk
shots.reason: Several deliberate brush leaves establish a calm opening.
shots.rights_note: Public Domain Mark 1.0 — US Army Air Forces production, National Archives Identifier 64512.
shots.source_caveat: Same occupation-era caveat as the woodblock entries drawn from this reel — see arts-crafts-kyoto-woodblock-outline.

shots.title: Block Cutting and Printing — design transfer
shots.reason: Transferred motif becomes a stronger pencil contour.
shots.rights_note: No explicit licence statement on the item page. Same Ephemeral Films collection-presumption basis as block-cutting-printing-carving-1950 — see that entry's caveat.
shots.source_caveat: A different moment (the design-transfer step) in the same reel as block-cutting-printing-carving-1950.

shots.title: The Violin Maker of Cremona
shots.reason: The maker lifts, turns and inspects the violin.
shots.rights_note: US PD — pre-1923 Biograph theatrical release; no rights statement on the item page beyond age-based PD.
shots.source_caveat: Narrative fiction (D.W. Griffith, Biograph), not documentary — the workshop and instrument-building gesture are staged, and most of the film is a courtship/contest plot with the workshop as backdrop rather than a documented process. A full contact-sheet review found this the weakest visual-bar fit of the pool's craft clips; used because instrument-making otherwise yielded only one clean candidate across every archive this pass checked.

shots.title: Printing (1947) — press run
shots.reason: A complete press cycle gives the middle its pulse.
shots.rights_note: Public Domain, per the archive.org item page.
shots.source_caveat: Same source film as printing-1947-composing, a different scene (~5:28 per the item's own shotlist, 'various printing presses in active operation').

shots.title: The Face of Lincoln
shots.reason: Working the brow, eye and nose lets the face emerge.
shots.rights_note: Public Domain, per the archive.org item page (USC Department of Cinema production).
shots.source_caveat: Named individual (Merrell Gage, USC sculpture department head, d. 1981) — historical, deceased, low personality-rights risk. The item page notes a separate paid HD master is available via A/V Geeks for broadcast use; the free download used here is the page's own stated public-domain file, not that paid product.

shots.title: Fantasmagorie — the animator's hand
shots.reason: The live hands arrange the figure, then the animated result completes a playful miniature story.
shots.rights_note: Public Domain Mark 1.0, per the archive.org item page (Émile Cohl, 1908).
shots.source_caveat: The rest of the 77-second film is pure line animation, not on-brief; this clip is the one live-action hand-and-materials insert. The white-on-black negative aesthetic reads as chalk-on-blackboard even though the medium is paper cutouts, which is why it's grouped here rather than under drawing.

grading: Monochrome; fixed per-shot 2nd/98th-percentile exposure levels mapped to 32–208. No automatic frame-by-frame exposure, so the film does not pump.
